 Jerusalem Post / Israel Election 2026 Smotrich presses Ofer Winter to drop Knesset run in exchange for Defense Ministry appointment
 The finance minister additionally stated that he would offer Winter a directorate for haredi (ultra-Orthodox) enlistment and integration into the workforce. 
 Follow us on Google Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich attends a press conference at the Finance Ministry in Jerusalem, July 1, 2026. ( photo credit : YONATAN SINDEL/FLASH90 ) By KESHET NEEV OCTOBER 21, 2026 17:04 Updated : OCTOBER 21, 2026 21:03 Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich on Wednesday offered People of Israel Party leader Ofer Winter a ministerial position in the Defense Ministry in exchange for withdrawing from the October 27 election, less than a week before Israelis head to the polls.
 The statement came as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Smotrich have both been pressuring Winter to withdraw from the election race; nonetheless, the People of Israel chairperson has asserted that he has no intention of resigning.
 The position would come from the ministerial allocation granted to Smotrich’s Religious Zionist Party as part of potential coalition negotiations.
 The far-right RZP, which is part of Netanayhu’s outgoing coalition, also stated that it would offer Winter the “full authority to establish a voluntary emigration directorate for Gaza,” on condition of withdrawing.
 The finance minister additionally stated that he would offer Winter a directorate for haredi (ultra-Orthodox) enlistment and integration into the workforce.
 Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich calls for People of Israel's Ofer Winter to drop out of the Knesset election race, unite the Right in return for a ministerial post, October 21, 2026. (Credit: Religious Zionist Party) Winter rejected Smotrich’s offer and calls from him to withdraw from the election in a statement made later in the evening.
 “You’ve got it wrong. We didn’t come for a job, as you’re accustomed to. We came to bring change and lead a new path,” Winter stated.
 “We came to serve those who serve, not to enable the continuation of political patronage and the division of positions. We will not surrender,” he added.
 Winter also said he would continue to be part of Netanyahu’s “right-wing bloc,” provided that a law enforcing conscription and supporting those who serve in the IDF is passed.
 Winter’s People of Israel Party has endorsed Netanyahu as prime minister. His party has recently been polling below or just above the required electoral threshold. Winter had stated he was seeking to be defense minister in the next government.
 Earlier on Wednesday, Winter said in a Channel 12 interview, when asked whether it was a mistake to endorse Netanyahu for prime minister so early in the campaign, that he sometimes considers “whether it was right or wrong.”
 However, he added: “That is irrelevant. I am a man of my word and part of the national camp.”
 People of Israel to continue endorsing Netanyahu for PM, Yoseph Haddad says 
 Yoseph Haddad, who holds the second slot on the People of Israel Knesset slate, subsequently stated that the party would continue to endorse Netanyahu as prime minister.
 “We in the People of Israel Party are people of our word. From the very beginning, party leader Ofer Winter said we would recommend Netanyahu for prime minister.”
 “That is what we will do, even as Netanyahu himself and others in the coalition walk all over us and act against us, and even after we are subjected to a campaign of smears, spin, and character assassination,” Haddad added.
 Netanayhu’s ruling Likud released a statement in which the prime minister directly addressed Winter, calling on him to withdraw.
 “Ofer Winter, you are not passing the electoral threshold in any of the polls. You promised to act responsibly and withdraw from the race if you endangered the right,” the prime minister stated.
 Netanyahu called on Winter to withdraw now to “save the right,” reiterating his earlier remarks that doing so would “prevent a dangerous left-wing government,” led by the opposition bloc seeking to replace the premier.
 The People of Israel Party has sought to bring together people who were never in the Knesset or part of the political or security failures surrounding the October 7 Hamas massacre in 2023.
 The prime minister has also repeatedly called on voters not to support smaller parties on the right, warning that splitting the right-wing vote could cost his camp the election.
